sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling of the complete observed path \(W=(X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,D)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(D\), with treatment beginning after date \(2\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every mixing, conditional assignment, and transition probability in the proposal-specific model lies in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical thirty-two-cell path PMF is inverted over all thirty-two labeled one-collision branches; no relative alignment is selected before projection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 identifies the model parameters under RSM, M, and ID; Proposition 5 and Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under the paper's stated TI--LT regular conditions.
Theorem 1 identifies type-specific initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities up to a common permutation from four consecutive observations under Assumptions 1--3.
Sections 3.2--3.4 formulate model comparison, implicit observable constraints, identification, and bounding for polynomial latent-variable models through real quantifier elimination.
Cylindrical algebraic decomposition gives an exact quantifier-elimination method for formulas over real closed fields.
CAD-based real quantifier elimination has doubly exponential worst-case dependence on dimension, while other real-algebraic methods address selected tasks with different bounds.
A rational inverse and semialgebraic membership conditions characterize regular parts of a single binary hidden Markov model, with exceptional cases treated as lower-dimensional submodels.
Discrete causal bounds can be posed as polynomial programs and approximated by spatial branch-and-bound with certified outer bounds and \(\epsilon\)-sharpness.
Finite mixtures are exactly partially identified under an excluded source of mixture-weight variation using probability restrictions.
Criterion inversion yields confidence regions for identified sets and their images under stated pointwise and uniform conditions.

tldr: On the compact binary four-period model, the completed singular result is the exclusive stratum with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. Terminal splitting reduces its forty-coordinate labeled fiber to sixteen ten-variable orientation/alignment charts for each collided state. A corrected full Collins certificate projects every pair in the complete polynomial family and exactly decides branch feasibility and aggregate-ATT constancy, including zero and box-face cells; it is a generic exact certificate, not the still-open compressed economic sign basis. The exact algorithm returns the attained, possibly disconnected sharp image with endpoint witnesses. Full-PMF inversion is uniformly honest in finite samples and remains auxiliary; no endpoint or Hausdorff consistency is claimed. An injective one-parameter family has two separated quotient ATT values, proving positive-dimensional persistence but not relative openness in a larger collision variety.

project_justification.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's parameter and ATT identification results impose their stated regular conditions, while Higgins and Jochmans require rank, type-separation, and connectivity conditions. Neither classifies aggregate ATT on the exclusive one-collided-control-row fiber. General Collins quantifier elimination can decide polynomial formulas, but an incomplete projection subfamily cannot certify simultaneous structural equalities, and generic CAD does not itself supply the causal chart reduction or a compressed economic diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: Exactly one collided control terminal row is the first completed nonregular stratum here: full-path terminal splitting, rank failure, compact-box contact, and the two relative cross-arm alignments interact but reduce to ten coordinates. The result deliberately does not claim the other fifteen terminal-collision patterns of a global atlas.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the corrected arm-label-aware ten-coordinate reconstruction, uses a complete all-pairs Collins projection certificate to classify feasibility and point identification on that stratum, computes its exact attained ATT image, and supplies auxiliary finite-sample full-PMF coverage. A separate injective one-parameter family proves persistent two-value ambiguity. Compression of the complete certificate to a smaller irredundant observable basis remains open.

related_work: Ahn--Kasahara is the closest econometric comparator in the same full-path latent-transition architecture; its regular identification results motivate the estimand and factorization here. The compact class \(\mathcal M_\eta\) and its exclusive one-collision stratum are not asserted to equal, contain, or extend that published identification class. Higgins and Jochmans give a four-observation Markov-mixture benchmark under rank, separation, and connectivity conditions but do not classify a two-arm one-collision alignment fiber. Critch motivates algebraic treatment of binary hidden Markov laws but has neither treatment-arm alignment nor this causal functional. Geiger--Meek and Collins provide generic real quantifier elimination; after correction, the paper uses the complete all-pairs projection machinery only after its model-specific forty-to-ten reduction and claims no generic complexity gain or compressed sign basis. Duarte and coauthors motivate polynomial causal bounds, whereas the object here is an exact attained semialgebraic image. Romano--Shaikh motivates identified-set inference; the present finite-sample inversion is auxiliary and makes no Hausdorff or endpoint-consistency claim.
interpretation: A reported ATT sign on this merger stratum is identified only when the complete two-copy certificate rejects every feasible unequal-ATT pair across all orientations and both relative alignments. Otherwise the estimand is the attained set itself, which may be disconnected and must not be replaced by its convex hull. The exact certificate is suitable as a backend audit trail; a short economically interpretable front-end diagnostic remains an open compression problem.
technical_internal_limitation: The completed algebra covers only laws whose entire compact fiber has distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one specified collided control terminal row. The certificate has now been repaired to project equality--equality and every other polynomial pair, but it remains full Collins quantifier elimination and may have its generic worst-case cost. No endpoint, Hausdorff, or branch-persistence consistency theorem is claimed. The positive-dimensional benchmark is one explicit affine family and is not claimed relatively open in the full collision variety.
honest_scope: Completed claims are quotient invariance, the corrected forty-to-ten one-collision reduction, the complete thirty-two-branch feasibility and ATT-constancy certificate across both collided states, the exact attained stratum-restricted region, the explicit positive-dimensional two-value family, and uniformly honest finite-sample full-PMF inversion. No result is claimed for the other terminal-collision strata, for an unboxed singular class, for a global sixteen-collision-pattern atlas, for relative openness of the benchmark family, or for Hausdorff or ordered-endpoint consistency. The complete certificate is not advertised as the model-specific compressed vanishing/sign test requested by the broader agenda; strict sufficient and irredundant compression remains the open question. No overlap, inclusion, or extension relation with Ahn--Kasahara's regular identification class is claimed.

novel.justification: Any data-generating process with nondegenerate latent shares, assignment probabilities, and transition rows satisfies this compact-interior restriction for some smaller rational \(\eta\). Rationality permits exact input encoding, while the box makes every stratum-restricted image attained. This condition is maintained independently and is not attributed to Ahn--Kasahara's common-support condition.

standard.name: Two-type first-order latent Markov path factorization with treatment-arm transition independence

novel.justification: The common box is credible in applications without nearly deterministic type shares, selection, or transitions. It is stronger than bounding treatment assignment alone and is maintained transparently to define a compact sensitivity model, not to claim coverage of the full published class.

The exclusive stratum contains observed laws for which every compatible compact-box representation has the same single control-row collision while the other three terminal rows remain distinct. Such pooling is natural when latent groups share one next-state probability but differ elsewhere. Exclusivity makes the named stratum a complete causal model rather than a selected representation and, by compactness of the global fiber, keeps its noncollided gaps bounded away from zero at each law.

definitions.name: Ten-variable terminal-splitting systems
definitions.construction:
For fixed \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), \(s\in\{-1,1\}^{3}\), and \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), first impose \(\chi_{0k_0}^{01}=\chi_{0k_0}^{10}=\chi_{0k_0}^{11}=0\) and set
\[
 v_{10k_0}=v_{20k_0}=\frac{N_0(0,0,k_0)}{H_0(0,0,k_0)}.
\]
Retain \(r_{ij}=R_{10}(i,j,k_0)\), set \(R_{20}(i,j,k_0)=H_0(i,j,k_0)-r_{ij}\), and, for each of the other three blocks, set
\[
 R_{1d}(i,j,k)=\frac{N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}H_d(i,j,k)}{v_{1dk}-v_{2dk}},
 \qquad R_{2d}(i,j,k)=H_d(i,j,k)-R_{1d}(i,j,k).
\]
The free coordinate is exactly
\[
 y=(v_{110},v_{210},v_{111},v_{211},v_{10,1-k_0},v_{20,1-k_0},r_{00},r_{01},r_{10},r_{11})\in\mathbb R^{10}.
\]
The system \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) contains the eight cleared equalities \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\), the four cleared equalities \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R)=0\), the three strict orientation signs \(s_{dk}(v_{1dk}-v_{2dk})>0\), the inequalities \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\geq\eta^5\), and both cleared signs \(q-\eta\geq0\) and \(U-q\geq0\) for every reconstructed primitive \(q\).  Reconstruction first uses the arm-local quantities
\[
 T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)=\sum_kR_{zd}(i,j,k),\qquad
 S_{zd}^{R}(i)=\sum_jT_{zd}^{R}(i,j),\qquad
 w_{zd}^{R}=\sum_iS_{zd}^{R}(i),
\]
\[
 u_{zd}^{R}=\frac{S_{zd}^{R}(1)}{w_{zd}^{R}},\qquad
 a_{zdi}^{R}=\frac{T_{zd}^{R}(i,1)}{S_{zd}^{R}(i)},\qquad
 \kappa_{zd3j}^{R}=\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}^{R}(0,j)}.
\]
It then maps arm-local labels to structural labels by taking treated component \(z\) and control component \(\sigma(z)\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 u_{z1}&=u_{z1}^{R},& u_{z0}&=u_{\sigma(z),0}^{R},&
 a_{zi}&=a_{z1i}^{R}=a_{\sigma(z),0,i}^{R},\\
 c_{z3j}&=\kappa_{z1,3,j}^{R},& b_{z3j}&=\kappa_{\sigma(z),0,3,j}^{R},&
 c_{z4k}&=v_{z1k},& b_{z4k}&=v_{\sigma(z),0,k},\\
 \pi_z&=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R}+p_1w_{z1}^{R},&
 e_z&=\frac{p_1w_{z1}^{R}}{\pi_z}.&&
 \end{aligned}
\]
The equality defining \(a_{zi}\) is imposed by \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R)=0\).  The box signs are imposed on all displayed structural primitives, equivalently on the corresponding arm-local primitives before relabeling.  Every cleared denominator is one of the explicitly positive quantities \(H_d,T_{zd}^{R},S_{zd}^{R},w_{zd}^{R},p_d,\pi_z\), or one of the orientation-signed nonzero terminal differences.

definitions.name: Observable one-collision sign certificate
definitions.construction:
Order \(y\) as displayed in Definition \(\mathrm{def:ten-variable-system}\).  For each \(s\), put into one finite polynomial family every equality polynomial and every weak- or strict-inequality boundary polynomial in \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\), after clearing only denominators whose positivity is recorded in that system.  At each eliminated coordinate apply the full Collins projection operator to the entire current family: adjoin contents, all coefficients and leading coefficients in that coordinate, discriminants, and resultants and signed principal subresultant coefficients for every unordered pair of distinct current polynomials.  Thus equality--equality, equality--inequality, and inequality--inequality pairs are all projected.  Replace the family by a square-free basis of these projection polynomials and continue recursively through all ten coordinates.  Adjoin the three observable collision minors and the two numerators expressing that the common collided-row terminal probability lies in \([\eta,U]\).

To test target constancy, for every \(s'\) and \(\sigma'\in\Sigma\), form an independent copy \(y'\), put all polynomials from both branch systems into a single family, and adjoin the numerator obtained, after multiplication by a common positive squared denominator, from
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^{4}\left[
 \tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right)
 -\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P\right)
 \right]^2>0.
\]
Apply the same full-family projection operator to every unordered pair at every stage and eliminate all coordinates in \((y,y')\).  The finite list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is the union, over all eight \(s\), all comparison labels \((s',\sigma')\), and the feasibility and nonconstancy formulas, of the resulting polynomials in the observable cells of \(P\) and \(\eta\).  Its certificate records the sign of every final projection polynomial and the complete signed Sturm--Habicht lifting table, including sections on which a coefficient or resultant vanishes.  Exact sign-invariant lifting decides feasibility and equality of both ATT coordinates across all branches; it retains a sample point for every accepted cell and, for every rejected formula, a finite lifting record in which each candidate cell has a first violated atomic sign.

definitions.name: Exact one-collision ATT algorithm
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) takes reduced rational encodings of \(\eta\) and the thirty-two cells of \(P\); enumerates exactly \(2\cdot2^3\cdot2=32\) labeled branches \((k_0,s,\sigma)\); builds each ten-variable system \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\); performs the fixed Collins projection and signed Sturm--Habicht lifting in \(\mathrm{def:observable-sign-certificate}\); and projects each retained cell through \(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P)\). The joint image is returned as a quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((\tau_3,\tau_4)\). Each marginal is returned as an ordered finite union of closed intervals and isolated points whose endpoints have a square-free integer polynomial, rational isolating interval, and Thom sign sequence. Every endpoint carries a reconstructed real-algebraic \(\psi\) and its \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) label; every discarded branch carries an exact sign or polynomial infeasibility certificate.

definitions.name: Exact one-collision persistence family
definitions.construction: For every \(\vartheta\in(-1/100,1/100)\), let \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from \(\psi^{\diamond}\) by replacing only \(c_{130}=3/10\) by \(c_{130}(\vartheta)=3/10+\vartheta\), and let \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\) by the identical replacement of its treated coordinate. All other primitive coordinates are unchanged. Define \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}=F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})\). Thus \(\psi^{\diamond}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond}\), \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), and \(P^{\diamond}_{0}=P^{\diamond}\).

definitions.name: Analytic certificate-compression handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathsf{CertificateHandle}\): eliminate the four collided-block split coordinates through the rank-one determinant equations, branch only on their signed subresultant gcd alternatives, and audit any reduced list against the complete \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\) sign table.

definitions.name: Finite-sample full-PMF inversion
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}=\bigcup_{Q\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}:\lVert Q-\widehat P_n\rVert_\infty\le\delta_n(\alpha)}\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(Q)\), where \(\delta_n(\alpha)=\sqrt{\log(64/\alpha)/(2n)}\)

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\), one has \(F(\sigma\psi)=P\) and \(\tau(\sigma\psi;P)=\tau(\psi;P)\). The map \(\bar\tau_P([\psi])=\tau(\psi;P)\) is therefore well defined on \(\Phi_\eta(P)\) and on every \(\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).
statements.justification: The causal image is meaningful only after simultaneous latent labels are removed without changing aggregate ATT.
statements.gap: Regular mixture identification is commonly stated up to labels, but the quotient-induced causal functional must still be checked before singular branch images are pooled.
statements.consumer: The public \(ak\) package may report endpoint witnesses with arbitrary latent labels without changing the reported ATT set.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\).  The box restriction gives \(B(e_z;d)\geq\eta\), so
\[
 p_d=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_zB(e_z;d)\geq\eta>0.
\]
Thus every posterior weight used below is defined.  The interpretation of the transition parameters and iterated expectation give
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_2(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-u_{z1})a_{z0}+u_{z1}a_{z1}=m_{z2},
\]
and, successively,
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_3(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-m_{z2})b_{z30}+m_{z2}b_{z31}=m_{z3},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_4(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-m_{z3})b_{z40}+m_{z3}b_{z41}=m_{z4}.
\]
Since \(w_{z1}=\mathbb P_\psi(Z=z\mid D=1)\), another application of iterated expectation yields
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_t(0)\mid D=1]=\sum_{z=1}^2w_{z1}m_{zt},\qquad t\in\{3,4\}.
\]
Consistency gives \(O_t(P)=\mathbb E_\psi[X_t(1)\mid D=1]\).  Consequently the structurally defined causal target is related to the observed law by
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_t(1)-X_t(0)\mid D=1]
 =O_t(P)-\sum_{z=1}^2w_{z1}m_{zt}=\tau_t(\psi;P).
\]
This establishes the causal interpretation rather than defining it by the observed law.

Under the simultaneous action, every type-indexed coordinate satisfies \(q_z(\sigma\psi)=q_{\sigma^{-1}(z)}(\psi)\).  Relabeling the finite sum in the definition of \(F\) therefore gives, cell by cell,
\[
 F(\sigma\psi)_{ijkld}
 =\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_{\sigma^{-1}(z)}B(e_{\sigma^{-1}(z)};d)
   B(u_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d};i)B(a_{\sigma^{-1}(z),i};j)
   B(\kappa_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d,3,j};k)B(\kappa_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d,4,k};l)
 =F(\psi)_{ijkld}=P_{ijkld}.
\]
The same relabeling shows
\[
 w_{z1}(\sigma\psi)=w_{\sigma^{-1}(z),1}(\psi),
 \qquad m_{zt}(\sigma\psi)=m_{\sigma^{-1}(z),t}(\psi).
\]
Hence
\[
 \tau_t(\sigma\psi;P)
 =O_t(P)-\sum_{z=1}^2w_{\sigma^{-1}(z),1}m_{\sigma^{-1}(z),t}
 =\tau_t(\psi;P).
\]
The box \(\Theta_\eta\) is itself invariant under this permutation.  Therefore \(\sigma\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(\tau\) is constant on every orbit.  This proves that \(\bar\tau_P\) is well defined on \(\Phi_\eta(P)\), and restriction proves the same assertion on \(\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).

statements.statement: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), terminal splitting induces a surjection from the union of the sixteen feasible \((s,\sigma)\) ten-variable solution sets \(\{y:\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\}\) onto \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\). Thus the forty-coordinate existential description in \((R,v)\in\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) is exactly reduced to six terminal coordinates and four prefix splits. Across \(k_0\in\mathcal A\) there are exactly thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches. Rank failures and all \(\eta\)-box contacts occur as zero or weak-sign cells inside these systems and create no omitted branch.
statements.justification: This theorem gives the auditable structural reduction for the exclusive one-collided-control-row fiber and now makes the swapped control-to-treated label map explicit.
statements.gap: Generic elimination does not expose the six terminal coordinates, four collided-prefix splits, eight rank-one equations, four cross-arm alignment equations, or the exact sixteen branches for a fixed collided state.
statements.consumer: A checker for the public \(ak\) package can reconstruct both relative alignments without silently pairing treated type \(z\) with the wrong control primitives.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\), \(k_0\), and \(P\) as in the theorem.  By \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the labeled global fiber is nonempty and every member has exactly the displayed control collision and the other three terminal differences nonzero.  For \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), define the arm-conditional latent prefix mass and terminal probability by
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j)B(\kappa_{zd3j};k),
 \qquad v_{zdk}^{\psi}=\kappa_{zd4k}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Summing first over latent type and then after multiplication by the conditional probability of \(X_4=1\) gives
\[
 H_d(i,j,k)=R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k),
 \qquad
 N_d(i,j,k)=v_{1dk}^{\psi}R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+v_{2dk}^{\psi}R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{2}
\]
Every Bernoulli factor in the model is at least \(\eta\).  Also \(p_d=\sum_z\pi_zB(e_z;d)\in[\eta,U]\).  Consequently
\[
 w_{zd}=\frac{\pi_zB(e_z;d)}{p_d}\geq\frac{\eta^2}{U}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)\geq\frac{\eta^5}{U}>\eta^5.
 \tag{3}
\]
This proves every positivity assertion used below.

At \((d,k)=(0,k_0)\), the defining collision gives \(v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}\).  Equation (2) therefore implies
\[
 N_0(i,j,k_0)=v_{10k_0}^{\psi}H_0(i,j,k_0).
\]
The three displayed collision minors vanish and, because \(H_0(0,0,k_0)>0\),
\[
 v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}
 =\frac{N_0(0,0,k_0)}{H_0(0,0,k_0)}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The four values \(R_{10}^{\psi}(i,j,k_0)\) remain free.  In every other block, the terminal difference is nonzero; solving the two linear equations in (2) gives
\[
 R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =\frac{N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}^{\psi}H_d(i,j,k)}{v_{1dk}^{\psi}-v_{2dk}^{\psi}},
 \qquad R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)=H_d(i,j,k)-R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{5}
\]
Choose the three entries of \(s\) to be the signs of these differences.  There are \(2^3\) possible orientations.

For each \((z,d,j)\), factorization (1) yields
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,0)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,1)
 -R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,1)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,0)=0,
 \tag{6}
\]
which gives the eight equations \(\rho_{zdj}=0\).  Label the treated arm components by \(z\), and let control arm-local component \(\sigma(z)\) represent the same structural type.  Sharing \(a_{zi}\) across arms and using (3) gives
\[
 \frac{T_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}
 =\frac{T_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}.
\]
Cross multiplication is legitimate and gives the four equations \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R^{\psi})=0\).  All reconstructed coordinates are the corresponding coordinates of \(\psi\), after the explicit control relabeling by \(\sigma\), and hence satisfy every box sign.  Equations (3)--(6) therefore put the six noncollided terminal probabilities and the four collided-block splits into one of the sixteen solution sets.  The corrected reconstruction returns \(\psi\).  This proves that the chart union maps onto the labeled fiber.

Conversely, let \(y\) satisfy \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\), and construct \(R\) and \(v\) from the splitting formulas.  The orientation signs make the three denominators in (5) nonzero.  The imposed lower bounds make every \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\), and hence every \(T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)\), \(S_{zd}^{R}(i)\), and \(w_{zd}^{R}\), positive.  The first identity in (2), which now holds by construction, yields \(\sum_z w_{zd}^{R}=1\).

For fixed \((z,d,j)\), positivity and \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) say that the two rows of the positive \(2\)-by-\(2\) array in \((i,k)\) have the same normalized \(k\)-distribution.  With
\[
 \kappa_{zd3j}^{R}=\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}^{R}(0,j)},
\]
one therefore has
\[
 R_{zd}(i,j,k)=T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)B(\kappa_{zd3j}^{R};k).
 \tag{7}
\]
The definitions of \(u_{zd}^{R}\) and \(a_{zdi}^{R}\) similarly give
\[
 T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)=w_{zd}^{R}B(u_{zd}^{R};i)B(a_{zdi}^{R};j).
 \tag{8}
\]
Because all \(S\)'s are positive, the four alignment equations are equivalent to
\[
 a_{\sigma(z),0,i}^{R}=a_{z1i}^{R}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Use the corrected reconstruction: structural type \(z\) takes its treated primitives from arm-local component \(z\), its control primitives from arm-local component \(\sigma(z)\), and the common quantity in (9) as \(a_{zi}\).  Finally set
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R}+p_1w_{z1}^{R},
 \qquad e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}^{R}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{10}
\]
All terms are positive, and
\[
 \pi_ze_z=p_1w_{z1}^{R},\qquad
 \pi_z(1-e_z)=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R},\qquad
 \sum_z\pi_z=p_0+p_1=1.
 \tag{11}
\]
The imposed box signs put every reconstructed structural primitive in \([\eta,U]\), so the reconstruction belongs to \(\Theta_\eta\).  Combining (7), (8), and (11) reconstructs the conditional prefix factors in \(F\).  The two identities (2) then reconstruct all cells with \(X_4=1\), and subtraction from \(H_d\) reconstructs those with \(X_4=0\).  Multiplication by \(p_d\) gives \(F(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y))=P\).  Equation (4) and the three strict orientation signs give exactly the required one-collision pattern.  Thus every chart solution reconstructs a member of \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).

There are two free terminal values in each of the three noncollided blocks and none in the collided block, whose common value is fixed by (4).  There are four free prefix splits in the collided block; all remaining entries of the original thirty-two-dimensional \(R\) are fixed by (2).  Hence the forty coordinates \((R,v)\) reduce to ten.  For fixed \(k_0\), there are eight orientations and two relative alignments, hence sixteen labeled branches; the two choices of \(k_0\) give thirty-two.  No rank matrix is inverted.  Rank failure is retained by (6), all vanishing coefficients are retained as zero polynomial cells, and box contacts are retained by weak inequalities.  The only divisions are by the positive quantities proved above or by an explicitly orientation-signed nonzero terminal difference.  Thus no listed boundary or rank case creates an omitted branch.

statements.statement: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), every \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the signed lists \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\), \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), are observable and finite.  For each \(\sigma\), their sign vectors and complete signed Sturm--Habicht lifting tables are necessary and sufficient for each of the eight oriented systems \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) to have a real solution.  After the two relative alignments are combined, \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) is a singleton if and only if every two-copy target-nonconstancy formula is rejected.  Equivalently, every accepted branch cell has zero oscillation in both reconstructed coordinates \(\tau_3\) and \(\tau_4\), and all accepted branch and alignment images coincide.  If this condition fails, the same certificate returns two accepted cells and reconstructed latent witnesses with unequal ATT vectors.  These equivalences include vanishing rank coefficients, alignment coincidences, and every compact-box face.
statements.justification: On positive-arm one-collision laws, the repaired complete projection and lifting table is an exact necessary-and-sufficient certificate for branch feasibility and ATT point identification.
statements.gap: The theorem supplies a complete generic algebraic decision certificate after dimension reduction, not a smaller irredundant collection of economically named observable minors; that compression remains open.
statements.consumer: Applied analyses can certify whether all feasible merger resolutions agree in both ATT coordinates and can retain explicit unequal-ATT witnesses when they do not.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\), \(k_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  A compatible structural representation exists.  Since every assignment probability is in \([\eta,U]\),
\[
 p_d=\sum_z\pi_zB(e_z;d)\geq\eta>0.
 \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are observable rational functions of the thirty-two cells of \(P\), with denominator \(p_d\).  Multiplying by positive powers of \(p_0p_1\) converts every atomic equality or sign in a branch formula into an equivalent polynomial sign condition in \((P,\eta,y)\).  The family is finite because each branch contains finitely many reconstructed primitives and polynomial conditions.

The corrected observable-certificate definition applies the full Collins projection to the entire current polynomial family at every eliminated coordinate.  In particular, it includes the resultant and signed principal subresultant data for every equality--equality pair, as well as for equality--boundary and boundary--boundary pairs.  By the cited CAD quantifier-elimination lemma, the resulting projection and signed lifting table is finite and sign-invariant for every original polynomial, including on zero sections.  Consequently, for every \((s,\sigma)\),
\[
 \exists y\;\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{at least one lifted cell satisfies every atomic sign of that branch.}
 \tag{13}
\]
Necessity holds because a solution occupies one sign-invariant cell.  Sufficiency holds because the retained sample point of an accepted cell satisfies the original conjunction.  Full pairwise projection is essential here: it preserves the simultaneous zero set of all twelve equality polynomials, rather than merely their intersections with inequality boundaries.  Coefficients, discriminants, pairwise resultants, and signed subresultants retain the same equivalence when a leading coefficient, multiple root, rank coefficient, or box-boundary polynomial vanishes.

The dimension-reduction theorem and quotient invariance give the exact image identity
\[
 \mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 =\bigcup_{s\in\{-1,1\}^{3}}\ \bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \left\{
 \tau\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right):
 \mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \right\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
This union is nonempty by membership in \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Two elements of the right side differ if and only if some two branch solutions \(y,y'\) satisfy
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^{4}\left[
 \tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right)
 -\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P\right)
 \right]^2>0.
 \tag{15}
\]
Every denominator in (15) is a product of the positive masses in the reconstruction and the three nonzero terminal differences.  Multiplying by a common squared denominator is therefore sign preserving.  The corrected definition applies the same complete projection and lifting procedure to the conjunction of both branch systems and this strict polynomial inequality, for every pair of labels.  The CAD lemma then says that a comparison formula is accepted exactly when such an unequal pair exists.

If all comparison formulas are rejected, no two elements in the nonempty union (14) differ, so the sharp image is a singleton.  This is equivalently zero within-cell and within-branch oscillation plus equality across all accepted branch and alignment images.  If one comparison formula is accepted, its two retained sample points reconstruct, by the dimension-reduction theorem, two members of the labeled fiber with unequal ATT vectors; quotient invariance shows that they also give two distinct values of the quotient image.  The lifting argument includes every zero section, so this dichotomy remains necessary and sufficient at rank deficiencies, alignment coincidences, and compact-box contacts.

statements.statement: For rational \(\eta\) and rational \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\), \(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) terminates after examining exactly thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches and returns, for each \(k_0\), exactly the attained joint image \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a quantifier-free semialgebraic formula. It returns each nonempty \(\mathcal I_{k_0,t}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points with Thom-encoded real-algebraic endpoints, a reconstructed feasible latent representation for every endpoint and isolated component, and an exact infeasibility certificate for every discarded branch. The theorem claims equivalence to Collins real quantifier elimination after the proved ten-coordinate reduction and claims no improvement in generic worst-case CAD complexity.
statements.justification: Complete projection after the ten-coordinate reduction returns the attained causal region without convexifying disconnected components.
statements.gap: General CAD does not itself provide this corrected causal reconstruction, fixed branch inventory, or latent endpoint-witness grammar.
statements.consumer: The public \(ak\) backend can report exact marginal components, algebraic endpoints, and a feasible representation attaining each reported boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\eta\) and the cells of \(P\) be rational, with \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Equation (12) makes both arm probabilities positive.  After clearing the recorded positive denominators, every branch is a finite polynomial sign system with rational coefficients and hence, after common rescaling, integer coefficients.  The algorithm enumerates
\[
 2\cdot2^3\cdot2=32
\]
labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\).  The cited CAD lemma, applied with the corrected complete projection family, proves termination of each fixed finite projection-and-lifting computation and therefore of the finite loop.

There is a unique \(k_*\in\mathcal A\) for which \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_*}^{1\mathrm c}\): membership for both values would require the same global fiber to have a collision at each control terminal state while also having the other state distinct.  For \(k_0=k_*\), the dimension-reduction theorem and (14) show that the disjunction of accepted branch images is exactly \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  For \(k_0\ne k_*\), any accepted chart would, by positivity and its eight \(\rho\)-equations, factor \(R\) as in (7)--(8); its four \(\gamma\)-equations would align the arms as in (9); and its weight reconstruction (10)--(11) and terminal split identities would give a structural vector in \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  This would contradict \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_*}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Hence every wrong-state chart is rejected and both its branch union and \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) are empty.  Thus, for each \(k_0\), the algorithm returns the exact image rather than an outer approximation.

Introduce two retained coordinates \((q_3,q_4)\), adjoin
\[
 q_t=\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right),
 \qquad t\in\{3,4\},
 \tag{16}
\]
clear only positive denominators, and eliminate \(y\).  The CAD lemma yields an equivalent quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((q_3,q_4)\).  Taking the disjunction over accepted labels proves the asserted exact joint formula.

For attainment, \(\Theta_\eta\) is compact and \(F\) is continuous, so
\[
 K(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}
\]
is compact.  If \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), exclusivity gives \(K(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), and hence \(K(P)=\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  The denominator \(p_1\) in \(w_{z1}\) is at least \(\eta\), while the counterfactual recurrences are polynomial in the primitive probabilities.  Thus \(\psi\mapsto\tau(\psi;P)\) is continuous on \(K(P)\).  Its joint image and both coordinate images are compact, and every extreme coordinate value is attained.

Each marginal is semialgebraic by (16) and quantifier elimination.  Collect the finitely many nonzero univariate polynomials appearing in its quantifier-free formula.  Their real roots partition \(\mathbb R\) into finitely many points and open intervals on which every atomic sign is constant.  Compactness therefore makes the selected set a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points.  Rational input makes every boundary root real algebraic.  Square-free factorization, rational root isolation, derivative-sign evaluation, and the signed lifting table produce a square-free integer polynomial, a rational isolating interval, and a Thom sign sequence for each endpoint.

For an endpoint \(q_t\), compactness supplies a point of \(K(P)\) attaining it.  Dimension reduction places that point in an accepted labeled branch.  Equivalently, CAD applied with the section \(q_t\) in (16) lifts to a real-algebraic \(y\); the corrected relabeling reconstruction yields a feasible real-algebraic structural endpoint witness.  If a branch is discarded, completeness of sign-invariant lifting means that every candidate cell violates at least one atomic sign.  Recording the first such atom in every candidate cell gives the finite exact infeasibility certificate promised by the algorithm.  The procedure is precisely real quantifier elimination after the proved ten-coordinate reduction.  Since neither the projection operator nor its generic schedule has been shortened, no improvement in generic worst-case CAD complexity follows.

statements.statement:
For every rational \(0<\eta<3/20\) and every real \(\vartheta\) with \(|\vartheta|<1/100\), one has \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta},\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\in\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\) and
\[
F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})=F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta})=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}.
\]
The labeled global fiber is
\[
\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
=\{\sigma\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}
\cup\{\sigma\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}.
\]
Consequently the global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and have exactly the two classes represented by \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) and \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\). Their ATT vectors are, respectively,
\[
\left(\frac{9}{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},-\frac{33}{2500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\left(-\frac{1}{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},\frac{49}{5000}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right).
\]
Thus each marginal sharp image consists of the corresponding two displayed coordinates, with gaps \(19/500\) and \(23/1000\). The map \(\vartheta\mapsto P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) is affine and injective. Its image is therefore a positive-dimensional persistence family inside the one-collision model, and it contains a dense rational subfamily. At \(\vartheta=0\) this gives \(\mathcal I_{0,3}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-1/500,9/250\}\) and \(\mathcal I_{0,4}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-33/2500,49/5000\}\). No relative-openness claim in a larger collision variety is made.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,3/20)\) and \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta|<1/100\). We first verify the probability box and equality of the two observed laws. The only perturbed primitive satisfies
\[
 \frac{29}{100}<\frac{3}{10}+\vartheta<\frac{31}{100}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Every other primitive of either representation lies in \([1/5,4/5]\). Since \(\eta<3/20<1/5\) and \(U=1-\eta>17/20>4/5\), (1) proves that both representations lie strictly inside \(\Theta_\eta\).

For \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\), the arm probabilities and posterior type weights are
\[
 p_1=\frac12\frac35+\frac12\frac25=\frac12,
 \qquad p_0=\frac12,
 \qquad (w_{10},w_{20})=\left(\frac25,\frac35\right),
 \qquad (w_{11},w_{21})=\left(\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{2}
\]
For \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\), the type probabilities are \((3/5,2/5)\) and both assignment probabilities are \(1/2\). Hence its posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\) in both arms. The two representations have identical treated components with identical treated weights. In the control arm, the second representation pairs weight \(3/5\) with the former second component and weight \(2/5\) with the former first component. Commutativity of this two-term mixture, applied directly to the definition of \(F\), therefore gives
\[
 F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,ijkld}
 \quad\text{for every }i,j,k,l,d\in\mathcal A.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next prove that (3) exhausts the global fiber. For a fixed arm \(d\), define the observable \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrices, with row index \(l\) and column index \(i\), by
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}(l,i)=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
\]
In any two-type representation of this conditional law, put \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{zd3j}\), \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{zd4k}\), let \(V_k\) have column \(z\) equal to \((1-v_{zk},v_{zk})^{\mathsf T}\), and set
\[
 S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j).
\]
The full-path factorization gives, entry by entry,
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}=V_k\operatorname{diag}\bigl(B(q_{1j};k),B(q_{2j};k)\bigr)S_j.
 \tag{4}
\]

Consider the treated arm. In its displayed representation,
\[
 |\det V_0|=\frac35,
 \qquad |\det V_1|=\frac25,
 \tag{5}
\]
and, because both types have \(a_{z0}=3/10\), \(a_{z1}=4/5\),
\[
 \det S_j=w_{11}w_{21}B(3/10;j)B(4/5;j)(u_{21}-u_{11}),
\]
so that
\[
 \det S_0=\frac{21}{3125},
 \qquad \det S_1=\frac{36}{3125}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Every factor \(B(q_{zj};k)\) in (4) is at least \(1/5\) throughout \(|\vartheta|<1/100\). Equations (4)--(6) imply the uniform recovery-minor bound
\[
 |\det Q_{jk}^{1}|\ge
 \frac25\left(\frac15\right)^2\frac{21}{3125}
 =\frac{42}{390625}>0.
 \tag{7}
\]
Thus all four treated matrices are invertible. Moreover,
\[
 Q_{01}^{1}(Q_{00}^{1})^{-1}Q_{10}^{1}(Q_{11}^{1})^{-1}
 =V_1\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1(\vartheta),\lambda_2)V_1^{-1},
 \tag{8}
\]
where direct cancellation in (4) yields
\[
 \lambda_1(\vartheta)
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/10+\vartheta)}{\operatorname{odds}(7/10)}
 =\frac{3(3+10\vartheta)}{7(7-10\vartheta)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_2
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/5)}{\operatorname{odds}(1/5)}=6.
 \tag{9}
\]
For \(|\vartheta|<1/100\), monotonicity of the first rational function gives
\[
 0<\lambda_1(\vartheta)<\frac{31}{161},
 \qquad
 (\lambda_2-\lambda_1(\vartheta))^2>\left(\frac{935}{161}\right)^2>0.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus the two eigenvalues in (8) are distinct, uniformly along the family. The two one-dimensional eigenspaces of the observable matrix in (8) are consequently exactly the two columns of \(V_1\); normalizing each probability column to sum to one recovers \(V_1\) up to permutation. Next,
\[
 Q_{00}^{1}(Q_{01}^{1})^{-1}V_1
 =V_0\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{1-q_{10}}{q_{10}},\frac{1-q_{20}}{q_{20}}\right),
 \tag{11}
\]
so column normalization recovers \(V_0\) in the same order. Finally,
\[
 S_j=V_0^{-1}Q_{j0}^{1}+V_1^{-1}Q_{j1}^{1}.
 \tag{12}
\]
The two summands on the right of (12) equal \(\operatorname{diag}(1-q_{1j},1-q_{2j})S_j\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(q_{1j},q_{2j})S_j\), respectively. Their row sums recover \(q_{zj}\); summing \(S_0+S_1\) and taking positive-mass ratios recovers \(w_{z1}\), \(u_{z1}\), and \(a_{zi}\). Because (7) is observable, every alternative treated decomposition has invertible factors in (4), so the same argument applies to it. Hence the treated decomposition is unique up to type permutation. In particular, every globally compatible representation has
\[
 a_{10}=a_{20}=\frac3{10},
 \qquad a_{11}=a_{21}=\frac45.
 \tag{13}
\]

The control conditional law is independent of \(\vartheta\). Define the observable quantities
\[
 g_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
 \qquad
 h_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
\]
All conditioning events have positive probability by the strict probability box. Exact evaluation from (3) gives
\[
 (g_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}41/115&111/230\\[2pt]23/45&11/30\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 (h_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}103/575&174/575\\[2pt]49/225&14/75\end{pmatrix},
 \tag{14}
\]
and
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\frac12
 \quad\text{for every }i,j.
 \tag{15}
\]
In an arbitrary compatible control decomposition, let \(\lambda_i=P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0)\), \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{z0,3,j}\), and \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{z0,4,k}\). Equation (13) makes \(Z\) conditionally independent of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,D=0)\), whence
\[
 g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
 \tag{16}
\]
The two observable row differences are
\[
 g_{00}-g_{10}=-\frac{32}{207},
 \qquad g_{01}-g_{11}=\frac8{69}.
 \tag{17}
\]
By (16), (17) implies \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\) and \(q_{1j}\ne q_{2j}\) for both \(j\). Multiplying (15) by the positive conditional probability of \(X_3=0\) gives, for \(i=0,1\),
\[
 \lambda_i(1-q_{1j})(v_{10}-1/2)
 +(1-\lambda_i)(1-q_{2j})(v_{20}-1/2)=0.
 \tag{18}
\]
The determinant of the two equations (18) is
\[
 (\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(1-q_{1j})(1-q_{2j})\ne0,
\]
because the compact box has \(q_{zj}<1\). Therefore
\[
 v_{10}=v_{20}=\frac12.
 \tag{19}
\]

For the noncollided terminal row, (14), (16), and (17) give
\[
 \beta_j=\frac{h_{0j}-h_{1j}}{g_{0j}-g_{1j}},
 \qquad (\beta_0,\beta_1)=\left(\frac14,1\right),
\]
and
\[
 h_{ij}-\beta_jg_{ij}=c_j,
 \qquad (c_0,c_1)=\left(\frac9{100},-\frac9{50}\right).
 \tag{20}
\]
Because \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\), equality of the two affine mixtures in (20) forces the corresponding component equalities
\[
 q_{z0}(v_{z1}-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\frac9{50}
 \quad (z=1,2).
 \tag{21}
\]
Likewise, the two observed identities \(g_{i1}=3(1-g_{i0})/4\), together with (16) at the two distinct values \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\), imply
\[
 q_{z1}=\frac34(1-q_{z0})
 \quad (z=1,2).
 \tag{22}
\]
Writing \(x=q_{z0}\) and \(v=v_{z1}\), equations (21)--(22) become
\[
 x(v-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad (1-x)(1-v)=\frac6{25}.
\]
Eliminating \(x\) gives
\[
 50v^2-55v+14=(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
 \tag{23}
\]
The discriminant in (23) is \(225>0\). Since (17) forbids the two types from using the same root, the unordered control triples are exactly
\[
 (q_{z0},q_{z1},v_{z1})
 \in\left\{
 \left(\frac35,\frac3{10},\frac25\right),
 \left(\frac15,\frac35,\frac7{10}\right)
 \right\}.
 \tag{24}
\]
For the second triple in (24), (14) and (16) give \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=(14/23,2/9)\). Since \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=0\mid D=0)=23/50\), its control weight and initial-state probability are
\[
 w_{10}=\frac{23}{50}\frac{14}{23}+\frac{27}{50}\frac29=\frac25,
 \qquad
 u_{10}=\frac{(27/50)(2/9)}{2/5}=\frac3{10}.
 \tag{25}
\]
The other component consequently has weight \(3/5\) and initial-state probability \(7/10\). This recovers the displayed control decomposition up to permutation. For completeness, the two determinants in (18), under the labeling used in (25), are the fixed values
\[
 \frac{128}{1035}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{112}{1035},
 \tag{26}
\]
while (17), (23), and (26) show explicitly that every treated and control recovery minor or discriminant used in the argument is uniformly nonzero along the entire family.

The treated and control arm decompositions are now separately unique up to permutation. There are exactly two relative alignments. Indeed, the identities following from the definition of posterior weights are
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{z0}+p_1w_{z1},
 \qquad e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Pairing control weights \((2/5,3/5)\) with treated weights \((3/5,2/5)\) in the displayed order gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/2,1/2)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(3/5,2/5)\). Crossing the pairing gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(3/5,2/5)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(1/2,1/2)\). Both solutions have strict box slack, and (27) leaves no third alignment.

For either relative alignment and either simultaneous labeling, the first terminal difference in the definition of \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\) is zero and the absolute values of the remaining three differences are
\[
 \left(\left|\frac7{10}-\frac25\right|,
 \left|\frac15-\frac45\right|,
 \left|\frac7{10}-\frac3{10}\right|\right)
 =\left(\frac3{10},\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{28}
\]
Thus every compatible representation is in \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\). Equations (3)--(28) prove that \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), that its labeled global fiber is precisely the simultaneous permutations of the two displayed representations, and that the global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and contain exactly two classes.

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\), \(\tau\) is invariant under every simultaneous type permutation, so it remains only to evaluate one representative of each of these two quotient classes. For the displayed alignment, the untreated recursions in the definition of \(\tau\) give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac25,\frac{29}{50}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{21}{50},\frac{229}{500}\right).
 \tag{29}
\]
Only the type-one treated transition out of \(X_2=0\) varies. By (2) and \(P(X_2=0\mid Z=1,D=1)=1-m_{12}=1/2\), the observed treated mean at date \(3\) is
\[
 O_3(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\frac{111}{250}+w_{11}(1-m_{12})\vartheta
 =\frac{111}{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10}.
 \tag{30}
\]
For type one the treated date-four transition difference is \(c_{141}-c_{140}=7/10-1/5=1/2\). Therefore
\[
 O_4(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\frac{259}{500}+w_{11}(1-m_{12})(c_{141}-c_{140})\vartheta
 =\frac{259}{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}.
 \tag{31}
\]
For the crossed alignment, the corresponding untreated recursions are
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac9{20},\frac{91}{200}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{11}{25},\frac{147}{250}\right).
 \tag{32}
\]
The untreated quantities in (29) and (32) do not depend on \(\vartheta\). Weighting by \((3/5,2/5)\) gives, respectively,
\[
 \left(\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z3},\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z4}\right)
 =\left(\frac{51}{125},\frac{332}{625}\right)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(\frac{223}{500},\frac{2541}{5000}\right).
 \tag{33}
\]
Subtracting these two vectors from (30)--(31) gives
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(\frac9{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
 -\frac{33}{2500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right),
 \tag{34}
\]
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(-\frac1{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
 \frac{49}{5000}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right).
 \tag{35}
\]
The exhaustion of the quotient fiber proves that these two vectors, and only these two vectors, form the sharp joint image. Their date-three gap is \(19/500\), and their date-four gap is \(23/1000\), independently of \(\vartheta\). Hence the asserted marginal two-point sets and their specialization at \(\vartheta=0\) follow.

Finally, the full observed cell with \((i,j,k,l,d)=(0,0,1,1,1)\) obeys
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,00111}-P^{\diamond}_{0,00111}
 =\left(\frac12\frac35\frac35\frac7{10}\frac7{10}\right)\vartheta
 =\frac{441}{5000}\vartheta.
 \tag{36}
\]
Thus \(\vartheta\mapsto P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) is affine and injective. Its image is a nondegenerate one-dimensional open affine segment in the one-collision model. For rational \(\vartheta\), every primitive and hence every cell of \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) is rational; the rational parameters are dense in the interval. This proves positive-dimensional rational persistence of the two separated ATT classes. Equation (36) does not imply, and the proposition does not assert, relative openness in any larger collision variety.
statements.justification: An explicit injective one-parameter family proves that the disconnected two-value geometry persists on a positive-dimensional subset rather than occurring at one isolated observed law; it makes no claim of relative openness in the full collision variety.
statements.gap: Generic label switching does not establish a causal ATT gap after quotienting simultaneous labels, and the cited mixture papers provide no exact one-collision persistence family with two aggregate-ATT values.
statements.consumer: Regression tests for the public package can follow the rational parameter path, verify both branch witnesses and their fixed ATT gaps, and prevent replacement of the attained two-point set by its interval hull.

statements.statement: Under independent multinomial sampling, for every \(n\ge1\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}}P^n\{\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\}\ge1-\alpha\). The event covers both marginal identified sets simultaneously. No endpoint-consistency, Hausdorff-consistency, or branch-persistence conclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: This auxiliary appendix-tier theorem covers the entire disconnected identified set uniformly at every sample size by inverting the full empirical PMF.
statements.gap: Finite-sample outer coverage alone does not imply branch persistence or set-estimation consistency; those conclusions require the separate explicit continuity conditions.
statements.consumer: Applied analyses obtain honest simultaneous coverage of both marginal sets without selecting one latent alignment.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(w\) and put \(Y_r=\mathbf 1\{W_r=w\}\) and \(q=P(w)\).  Under independent multinomial sampling, the \(Y_r\)'s are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(q\).  For every real \(\lambda\),
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{\lambda(Y_r-q)\}
 =(1-q)e^{-\lambda q}+qe^{\lambda(1-q)}
 \leq e^{\lambda^2/8}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, if \(K\) is the logarithm of the middle expression, exponential tilting remains Bernoulli, so \(K(0)=K'(0)=0\) and \(K''(\lambda)=q_\lambda(1-q_\lambda)\leq1/4\).  Taylor's formula with integral remainder proves (17).

For any nonnegative \(Z\) and \(a>0\), \(\mathbf 1\{Z\geq a\}\leq Z/a\), so taking expectations gives \(P\{Z\geq a\}\leq \mathbb E[Z]/a\).  Apply this inequality to the exponential of the centered sum.  Independence and (17), for \(\lambda>0\), give
\[
 P^n\{\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)\geq\delta\}
 \leq\exp\{-\lambda n\delta+n\lambda^2/8\}.
\]
Choosing \(\lambda=4\delta\) and applying the same calculation to \(-Y_r\) gives
\[
 P^n\{|\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)|>\delta\}\leq2e^{-2n\delta^2}.
 \tag{18}
\]
There are thirty-two observed cells.  The union bound and the stated value of \(\delta_n(\alpha)\) yield, uniformly over all multinomial laws,
\[
 P^n\{\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty>\delta_n(\alpha)\}
 \leq64\exp\{-2n\delta_n(\alpha)^2\}=\alpha.
 \tag{19}
\]
On the complementary event, the true \(P\), which by hypothesis belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), is one of the laws \(Q\) in the union defining \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\).  Therefore the whole sharp set \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), rather than a selected latent value, is contained in \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\).  Taking probabilities in (19) and then the infimum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}}
 P^n\{\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]
Projection of this one joint containment event covers both marginal identified sets simultaneously.  The radius tends to zero, but fixed-coverage containment alone supplies neither lower hemicontinuity nor branch persistence; hence it does not by itself imply the endpoint or Hausdorff conclusions excluded by the theorem.

statements.statement: Can the complete Collins projection list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\) be reduced to a strictly smaller, economically interpretable and irredundant collection of observable minors and signed resultants that still determines branch feasibility and singleton aggregate ATT on \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\)? Establish sufficiency of the reduced list and prove irredundancy by constructing, for every retained sign, two rational laws agreeing on all other proposed signs but differing in feasibility or ATT constancy.
statements.justification: The exact certificate is finite and computable, but a minimal observable diagnostic would reveal which empirical path restrictions actually govern point identification.
statements.gap: Neither general CAD theory nor latent-mixture identification results isolate an irredundant causal sign basis for this one-collision stratum.
statements.consumer: The public \(ak\) interface could replace a large algebraic certificate by a concise diagnostic explaining which observed cell relation creates the ATT ambiguity.

obligation.what_is_open: A strictly smaller economically interpretable sign basis, together with a proof that it is sufficient and irredundant on the whole one-collision law class.
obligation.obstruction: The complete projection family contains coefficients and subresultants introduced for sign-invariance rather than obviously essential model restrictions. The frozen primitives provide no argument that a proposed deletion preserves every zero, rank-deficient, alignment, and box-contact branch, and no rational perturbation family establishes sign-by-sign necessity.
obligation.attempted: The collided-block rank equations were used first to remove the four free splits, and the remaining gcd alternatives were organized by their signed subresultants. This proves a valid compression route but does not certify a strict deletion: several projection signs co-vanish on the model's support variety, so changing one while holding all others fixed may itself be infeasible.
obligation.partial_result: The complete list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\), together with its signed lifting table, is finite, observable, and necessary and sufficient for feasibility and singleton aggregate ATT by the observable-classification theorem.  The binary terminal split reduces the problem to ten variables and twelve structural equalities, and eliminating the four collided-block splits first through \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) is valid on every positive-mass branch.  What remains unproved is that a strict subset of the resulting projection signs is sufficient and that every retained sign is essential.

statements.statement: For every finite family of real polynomials, a finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to that family can be computed. Its cylindrical lifting decides every Boolean combination of their sign conditions, yields an equivalent quantifier-free formula after projection, and represents sections by continuous semialgebraic real-root functions. For rational input, real-algebraic sample points and boundary roots admit square-free polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom derivative-sign encodings.
